claim: Automation bias is well-established: decision makers favor automated suggestions over contradictory human information even when the automated advice is incorrect
source_citation: Mosier, K. L., & Skitka, L. J. (1996). Human decision makers and automated decision aids: Made for each other? In Automation and Human Performance, pp. 201-220.
notes: Foundational literature identifying errors of omission and commission across aviation and healthcare.

claim: Automation bias manifests through errors of omission (failing to notice an automated aid missed a hazard) and errors of commission (following a wrong automated recommendation over contradictory evidence)
source_citation: Mosier, K. L., & Skitka, L. J. (1996). Human decision makers and automated decision aids: Made for each other? In Automation and Human Performance, pp. 201-220.
notes: Core empirical taxonomy of automation failure modes.

claim: Automating the decision-selection stage of human-automation interaction produces the greatest degree of operator complacency and cognitive disengagement
source_citation: Parasuraman, R., Sheridan, T. B., & Wickens, C. D. (2000). A model for types and levels of human interaction with automation. IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics - Part A, 30(3), 286-297.
notes: Empirical synthesis of 4 automation stages: acquisition, analysis, selection, action.

claim: Calibrated trust occurs when subjective confidence matches actual system capability; overtrust produces misuse, undertrust produces disuse
source_citation: Lee, J. D., & See, K. A. (2004). Trust in automation: Designing for appropriate reliance. Human Factors, 46(1), 50-80.
notes: Definitional framework for trust calibration and behavioral reliance.

claim: Automation bias manifests across modern AI-driven enterprise work environments in 35 peer-reviewed studies (2015-2025)
source_citation: Systematic PRISMA review (2025). Automation bias in modern AI-driven work environments (35 studies, 2015-2025). AI & Society.
notes: Synthesizes modern cognitive psychology, human factors, and HCI across recent enterprise AI deployments.

claim: Adding AI explanations does not consistently reduce user over-reliance and can increase over-reliance on incorrect recommendations
source_citation: Bansal, G., Wu, T. S., Zhou, J., Fok, R., Nushi, B., Kamar, E., Ribeiro, M. T., & Weld, D. (2021). Does the whole exceed its parts? The effect of AI explanations on complementary team performance. CHI '21, Article 81, 1-16.
notes: Empirical demonstration that local feature-importance explanations can induce an illusion of system competence.

claim: Cognitive forcing functions compel active judgment before AI recommendations are revealed and significantly reduce over-reliance compared to explanation-only interfaces
source_citation: Bucinca, Z., Malaya, M. B., & Gajos, K. Z. (2021). To trust or to think: Cognitive forcing functions can reduce overreliance on AI in AI-assisted decision-making. Proc. ACM Hum.-Comput. Interact., 5(CSCW1), Article 188, 1-21.
notes: Evaluated multiple interaction designs; forced independent deliberation consistently mitigated automation bias.

claim: The reduction in AI over-reliance achieved by cognitive forcing functions is significantly moderated by an individual's Need for Cognition (NFC)
source_citation: Bucinca, Z., Malaya, M. B., & Gajos, K. Z. (2021). To trust or to think: Cognitive forcing functions can reduce overreliance on AI in AI-assisted decision-making. Proc. ACM Hum.-Comput. Interact., 5(CSCW1), Article 188, 1-21.
notes: Participants with higher intrinsic motivation for cognitive effort benefited more from forced deliberation.

claim: Cognitive offloading is well-documented in human memory and spatial navigation (transactive memory with search engines and GPS)
source_citation: Risko, E. F., & Gilbert, S. J. (2016). Cognitive offloading. Trends in Cognitive Sciences, 20(9), 676-688.
notes: Foundational cognitive review of external artifact utilization to reduce working memory load.

claim: Longitudinal cognitive deskilling and loss of analytical capability from prolonged generative AI usage occurs at scale
source_citation: [UNVERIFIED — NEEDS SOURCE]
source_url_or_doi: N/A (No verifiable longitudinal empirical study available)
notes: Theoretically plausible extension of offloading research, but lacks high-quality longitudinal empirical evidence; classified as an open research gap.

claim: Mindfulness meditation improves executive attention with small, consistent effects: Hedges' g = 0.29 for interventions and g = 0.32 comparing long-term meditators to non-meditators
source_citation: Sumantry, D., & Stewart, K. E. (2021). Meditation, mindfulness, and attention: A meta-analysis. Mindfulness, 12(6), 1332-1349.
notes: Effects concentrated narrowly in conflict inhibition and executive control.

claim: Mindfulness meditation in healthy adults has a small overall effect (g = 0.20) with modest effects on attention/executive control, but no significant effect on working memory
source_citation: Yakobi, O., Smilek, D., & Danckert, J. (2021). The effects of mindfulness meditation on attention, executive control and working memory in healthy adults: A meta-analysis of RCTs. Cognitive Therapy and Research, 45(4), 543-560.
notes: Meta-analysis restricted to randomized controlled trials in healthy adult populations.

claim: Mindfulness meditation produces small improvements in executive attention but limited or inconsistent evidence for alerting or orienting attention networks
source_citation: Sharpe, P. (2021). The effects of mindfulness meditation on attention regulation (Doctoral thesis). University of Plymouth.
notes: Doctoral meta-analysis and primary experimental series yielding null effects on alerting/orienting.

claim: The number of formal in-class meditation sessions, but not total intervention hours, significantly moderates attentional effect sizes
source_citation: Yakobi, O., Smilek, D., & Danckert, J. (2021). The effects of mindfulness meditation on attention, executive control and working memory in healthy adults: A meta-analysis of RCTs. Cognitive Therapy and Research, 45(4), 543-560.
notes: Authors suggest session count reflects participant compliance and motivation rather than purely neurobiological dose-response.

claim: Meditation programs show moderate evidence for anxiety (ES = 0.38 at 8 weeks), depression (ES = 0.30), and pain (ES = 0.33), but low evidence of any effect on attention specifically
source_citation: Goyal, M., Singh, S., Sibinga, E. M. S., et al. (2014). Meditation programs for psychological stress and well-being: A systematic review and meta-analysis. JAMA Internal Medicine, 174(3), 357-368.
notes: Rigorous systematic review of 47 RCTs (n = 3,515); found no evidence meditation outperforms active behavioral treatments; attention gains negligible.

claim: Human Development Index (HDI) geometric mean aggregation ignores net wealth distribution, quality-of-goods differences, and inequality
source_citation: UNDP (1990). Human Development Report technical notes. United Nations Development Programme.
notes: Recognized limitation leading to companion indices (IHDI, GII, MPI) to measure inequality.

claim: The Social Progress Index (SPI) equal weighting of 12 components assumes each contributes identically and independently to social progress without statistical or theoretical justification
source_citation: Jitmaneeroj, B. (2017). Beyond the equal-weight framework of the Social Progress Index: A quantile regression approach. International Journal of Social Economics, 44(12), 2336-2350.
notes: Demonstrated that equal weighting introduces distortion due to collinearity and unequal component impact.

claim: The Social Progress Index (SPI) components encode predominantly Western liberal normative assumptions, with lowest-ranked nations concentrated outside that framework
source_citation: Porter, M. E., Stern, S., & Green, M. (2017). Social Progress Index 2017: Methodological Report. Social Progress Imperative.
notes: Documented critique regarding the Opportunity and Inclusiveness pillars reflecting Western institutional models.

claim: World Happiness Report pooled OLS regression of national life evaluations against six determinants captures correlation rather than causal relationships
source_citation: Helliwell, J. F., Layard, R., & Sachs, J. (2018). World Happiness Report 2018. Sustainable Development Solutions Network.
notes: Single-item subjective wellbeing metric deliberately excluding normative evaluations of societal structure.

claim: Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) dual-cutoff counting method prevents high achievement in one dimension from compensating for acute deprivation in another
source_citation: Alkire, S., & Foster, J. (2011). Counting and multidimensional poverty measurement. Journal of Public Economics, 95(7-8), 476-487.
notes: Foundational methodology for non-compensatory identification of joint deprivation.

claim: Composite indicator development requires sensitivity and uncertainty analysis across weighting, normalization, and aggregation assumptions
source_citation: OECD & European Commission Joint Research Centre. (2008). Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators: Methodology and User Guide. OECD Publishing.
notes: Standard international econometric handbook for composite indicator auditing and uncertainty modeling.

claim: Intellectual humility can be reliably measured as cognitive and interpersonal willingness to acknowledge intellectual fallibility
source_citation: Leary, M. R., Diebels, K. J., Jongman-Sereno, K. P., et al. (2017). Cognitive and interpersonal features of intellectual humility. Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin, 43(6), 793-813.
notes: Psychometric validation of the Comprehensive Intellectual Humility Scale (CIHS).

claim: Cognitive Reflection Test (CRT) measures the disposition to override intuitive heuristic responses in favor of effortful reflection
source_citation: Frederick, S. (2005). Cognitive reflection and decision making. Journal of Economic Perspectives, 19(4), 25-42.
notes: Validated 3-item cognitive reflection measure; susceptible to test-retest familiarity contamination.

claim: The Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale (IUS-12) short form reliably measures cognitive, emotional, and behavioral reactions to ambiguous situations
source_citation: Carleton, R. N., Norton, M. P. J., & Asmundson, G. J. G. (2007). Fearing the unknown: A short version of the Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale. Journal of Anxiety Disorders, 21(1), 105-117.
notes: Validated 12-item bifactor scale measuring prospective and inhibitory anxiety.

claim: Metacognitive monitoring sensitivity can be quantified independently of response bias using type-2 signal detection (meta-d')
source_citation: Fleming, S. M., & Lau, H. C. (2014). How to measure metacognition. Frontiers in Human Neuroscience, 8, Article 443.
notes: Standard psychophysical framework for separating subjective confidence bias from objective metacognitive accuracy.

claim: AI literacy is measurable across affective, behavioral, cognitive, and ethical dimensions with strong internal reliability
source_citation: Ng, D. T. K., Luo, W., Chan, H. M. Y., & Chu, S. K. W. (2024). Design and validation of the AI literacy questionnaire. British Journal of Educational Technology, 55(3), 1082-1104.
notes: Validation of the 4-dimensional AI Literacy Questionnaire (AILQ) across student and adult cohorts.

claim: AI literacy conceptualization encompasses foundational knowledge, collaboration skills, and critical evaluation of societal impacts
source_citation: Ng, D. T. K., Leung, J. K. L., Chu, S. K. W., & Qiao, M. S. (2021). Conceptualizing AI literacy: An exploratory review. Computers and Education: Artificial Intelligence, 2, 100041.
notes: Literature synthesis establishing the conceptual taxonomy for multi-attribute AI competency.

claim: UNESCO AI competency frameworks define structured AI readiness across knowledge, skills, and values for students and educators
source_citation: UNESCO. (2024). AI Competency Framework for Teachers and AI Competency Framework for Students. UNESCO Publishing.
notes: Standardized international competency frameworks published by the United Nations.

claim: OECD/European Commission AI Literacy Framework structures competencies into system mechanics, human-AI collaboration, and societal impacts
source_citation: OECD & European Commission. (2026). AI Literacy Framework for Primary and Secondary Education. OECD Publishing.
notes: Multi-national curriculum benchmark establishing formal AI literacy dimensions.

claim: Autonomous decisional agency is empirically distinguishable from competence and technical capability
source_citation: Deci, E. L., & Ryan, R. M. (2000). The 'what' and 'why' of goal pursuits: Human needs and the self-determination of behavior. Psychological Inquiry, 11(4), 227-268.
notes: Self-Determination Theory (SDT) foundational distinction between volition (autonomy) and efficacy (competence).

claim: AI efficiency at optimizing means causally increases the human necessity for explicit clarity regarding normative ends
source_citation: [UNVERIFIED — NEEDS SOURCE]
notes: Philosophical and theoretical proposition; lacks direct empirical validation in human-AI interaction literature.

claim: A validated psychological index measuring readiness for AI cognitive asymmetry already exists in published scientific literature
source_citation: [UNVERIFIED — NEEDS SOURCE]
notes: Represents the core proposed research gap; no such composite instrument currently exists.

claim: Executive attention and conflict inhibition are reliably separable from alerting and orienting networks using the Attention Network Test (ANT)
source_citation: Fan, J., McCandliss, B. D., Sommer, T., Raz, A., & Posner, M. I. (2002). Testing the efficiency and independence of attentional networks. Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience, 14(3), 340-347.
notes: Neuropsychological task isolating executive conflict resolution, alerting, and spatial orienting.

claim: Subjective trust in automated systems diverges from objectively measured reliance behavior under decision pressure
source_citation: Lee, J. D., & See, K. A. (2004). Trust in automation: Designing for appropriate reliance. Human Factors, 46(1), 50-80.
notes: Reviews empirical literature warning against relying strictly on subjective trust questionnaires.

claim: Overlapping input and output pillars in innovation indices creates conceptual collinearity and risks tautological scoring
source_citation: WIPO, Cornell University, & INSEAD. (2020). Global Innovation Index 2020: Methodological and Statistical Audit. WIPO Publishing.
notes: Econometric audit detailing structural overlap between institutional inputs and creative outputs.

claim: Cross-cultural differences alter the construct meaning of individual autonomy and agency between individualist and collectivist frameworks
source_citation: Deci, E. L., & Ryan, R. M. (2000). The 'what' and 'why' of goal pursuits: Human needs and the self-determination of behavior. Psychological Inquiry, 11(4), 227-268.
notes: Cultural variation necessitates multi-group confirmatory factor analysis (MGCFA) invariance testing.

claim: AI sycophancy (models adapting output to agree with user biases) systematically reduces user critical verification and analytical scrutiny
source_citation: Sharma, M., Tong, M., Korbak, T., et al. (2023). Towards understanding sycophancy in language models. arXiv preprint arXiv:2310.13548.
notes: Demonstrates that models tailor arguments to match user preferences regardless of truth, degrading critical evaluation.

claim: Transactive memory and cognitive offloading to GPS navigation tools systematically reduces spatial environmental memory
source_citation: Risko, E. F., & Gilbert, S. J. (2016). Cognitive offloading. Trends in Cognitive Sciences, 20(9), 676-688.
notes: Established cognitive offloading effect replicated across spatial navigation trials.

claim: Equal weighting in multidimensional composite indices distorts relative country rankings when indicator correlations are strong
source_citation: Greco, S., Ishizaka, A., Tasiou, M., & Torrisi, G. (2019). On the methodological framework of composite indices: A review of the issues of weighting, aggregation, and robustness. Social Indicators Research, 141(1), 61-94.
notes: Econometric survey of aggregation flaws, showing that equal weighting implicitly assigns higher weight to correlated clusters.

claim: Providing automated explanations can induce user overconfidence through the illusion of explanatory depth
source_citation: Bansal, G., Wu, T. S., Zhou, J., et al. (2021). Does the whole exceed its parts? The effect of AI explanations on complementary team performance. CHI '21, Article 81, 1-16.
notes: Explanations generate a fluency heuristic that induces users to rationalize incorrect AI suggestions.
